verdicts.rewritten_summary: National-framework source (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): HRW, 29 Oct 2025, reports a leaked omnibus reform draft ("11th Judicial Package") that would amend the Turkish penal code to punish conduct "contrary to biological sex" with up to three years in prison and participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony with up to four; it would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25, mandate permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals, and expose both healthcare professionals performing such care and patients to criminal prosecution, with pretrial detention possible. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft; HRW calls for its withdrawal.

National-framework monitoring report (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): Kaos GL's Human Rights Report 2025, titled "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People", finds LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy, with instructions issued to public institutions under the "Year of the Family" banner. It documents 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected, 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (a striking increase over the prior year), 313 right-to-liberty violations - about 2.5 times the previous year - with 299 detention decisions, freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540, and 40 right-to-association violations including the first closure of an LGBTI+ association in many years.
